text:
The Market Explosion story
I was probably 6 or 8 bars away from the explosion. I heard the explosion and somebody, as i was running down somebody in English said bicycle bomb. There were no Americans hurt. I tried to stop the bleeding of a women by compressing the blood in and then someone else took over of Vietnamese. It was horrific, women and children were hurt bad. I didn't see any men there. There were 3 or 4 Americans running down with me, I didn't know any of them.
researchNotes: Told on 2026-09-12 under the heading "The Market Explosion story", a week after his son reported him saying, at the circled M on the Tu Do drawing (VD-0003), that the M stood for Market and that an explosion went off there, without being able to tell whether Larry had been present (2026-09-05-drawing-market-m, paraphrase). This is that story in his own words, and it settles the presence question in his telling: he was "probably 6 or 8 bars away" and ran toward it. KEPT APART FROM TWO OTHER SAIGON BOMBINGS HE HAS DESCRIBED, and not merged with either: the Embassy bombing of 30 March 1965, which he heard from "about a block away... at the Papillon" (2026-09-03), and the My Canh of 25 June 1965, where he was at the door (VN-0068). Details here that do not fit the Embassy bombing as documented are his own: a bicycle bomb, "no Americans hurt", women and children the casualties. He has also described giving first aid in a Saigon street after an explosion by a bar near the Palace, wrapping a man's bleeding throat in his T-shirt (VN-0120, 2026-09-03); here it is a woman whose bleeding he tried to stop. Whether those are one day told twice or two different days is not settled and is not put to him. Which market, and the date, are not yet searched. Ledger #35 and #36.
